title: Isolation of dermal adipocytes from mouse skin for biochemical analysis
protocol: Thaw individual single use corn oil tamoxifen aliquots.
Heat thawed corn oil tamoxifen aliquots at 37°C for 20 minutes.
Wrap tubes in tin foil to avoid light exposure.
Draw up 100 μL of corn oil tamoxifen solution into 1 mL syringes with 0.4 × 19 mm cannula.
Use individual syringes for each experimental mouse.
Inject 100 μL of corn oil tamoxifen solution intraperitoneally (i.p.) in each experimental mouse.
Repeat injection for five consecutive days.
Sacrifice the experimental mouse.
Shave the dorsal skin using an electric shaver.
Apply depilatory cream to the shaved skin for 1 minute.
Wash the skin with warm water and dry it with paper towels.
Clean the depilated skin with 70% ethanol.
Carefully cut out and excise the total dorsal skin.
Wash the skin twice by placing it in a 50 mL conical tube containing DMEM/F-12 media at 37°C.
Cut the skin into large coin-sized pieces.
Remove any extra tissues attached to the skin.
Float the skin on 5 mL digestion-mix in a 6 cm culture dish with the epidermal side up.
Incubate the floating skin in a 37°C cell incubator for 90–120 min.
Carefully remove the skin pieces from the digestion medium.
Transfer the pieces to a new 6 cm dish containing 3 mL 37°C DMEM/F-12 medium.
Gently dissociate the dWAT layer into the medium using a curved scalpel.
Pipette the cell suspension up and down using a pipette with truncated 1 mL tip.
Filter the dissociated cells through a 150 μm cell strainer into a new 50 mL conical tube.
Use truncated 1 mL pipette tips for transfer.
Carefully stir the solution by pipetting up and down in between transfers.
Wash the cell strainer with 2 mL DMEM/F12.
Ensure complete wetting of the entire sieve.
Filter the cell suspension through the washed strainer.
Work fast but handle the suspension with care.
Rinse through the strainer with fresh DMEM/F12, not exceeding a volume of 15 mL.
Transfer the cell mixture into a new 15 mL conical tube using truncated 1 mL pipette tips.
Centrifuge the tube at 600 × g for 5 min at 37°C.
Carefully transfer the floating dermal adipocytes to a 2 mL tube using a truncated 1 mL pipette tip.
Hold the pipette vertical and insert the tip only 1–2 mm lower than the lipid/adipocyte layer.
Take up only a small volume at a time.
Centrifuge the 2 mL tube at 200 × g at 37°C for 2 min.
Remove the underlying medium using a pipette with a thin tip.
Cool down centrifuge to 4°C.
Thaw previously frozen dermal adipocyte samples at 4°C.
Prepare protease inhibitor cocktail by diluting 1:100 in buffer A.
Dissolve one phosphatase inhibitor tablet in 10 mL of buffer A.
Add 250 μL of enzyme inhibitor mix to thawed dermal adipocyte sample.
Homogenize the mixture for 3 min at 30 Hz using MixerMill system with one stainless steel body per sample/tube.
Centrifuge homogenized samples at 350 × g at 4°C for 2 min.
Transfer supernatant to kit-provided pre-chilled −20°C filter cartridge with a collection tube.
Incubate the filter cartridge open at −20°C for 15–20 minutes.
Incubate the sample according to the kit manual.
Centrifuge at 350 × g for 2 min at 4°C with the cap open after incubation.
Perform BCA analysis to determine protein concentration.
Prepare protein standards according to the BCA datasheet.
Mix 50 parts of reagent A with 1 part of reagent B to prepare working reagent.
Pipette 25 μL of each standard and sample into a 96-well plate.
Add 200 μL of working reagent to each well and mix gently.
Incubate for 30 min at 37°C.
Cool the plate to 18°C–25°C after incubation.
Measure absorbance at 570 nm on a plate reader.
Add 1/10 of buffer B provided by the kit if not using ELISA or immune precipitation for downstream applications.
Mix LDS Sample buffer with sample in a ratio of 1:4 for loading.
Add 4% β-mercaptoethanol to the sample.
Heat up the mixture for 10 min at 75°C.
Cool on ice and spin down at 4°C after heating.
Freeze the sample at -80°C or proceed with SDS-PAGE.
Centrifuge 25 min at 4°C maximum speed to remove cell debris.
Prepare 4%–12% Bis-Tris NuPAGE gel by removing the white stripe.
Prepare 500 mL of SDS running buffer.
Put gel into the device and completely fill the Upper-Buffer-Chamber with SDS running buffer.
Fill the rest of the buffer into the Lower-Buffer-Chamber.
Remove the comb and wash pockets with SDS running buffer.
Load 20 μg protein in up to 40 μL sample per lane.
Load 10 μL of protein ladder.
Run gel at 130 V for approximately 70 min.
Soak 4 sponges and 8 sheets of filter paper in transfer buffer.
Activate PVDF-membrane in methanol (15–60 s) and soak in transfer buffer.
Put two sponges into the blotting chamber.
Place four filters into the blotting chamber.
Position the gel on top of the membrane in the blotting chamber.
Add another four filters to the blotting chamber.
Insert two more sponges into the blotting chamber.
Close the blotting chamber, put it into the device and fill with transfer buffer.
Fill the Lower-Buffer-Chamber with ice.
Blot for 105 min at 30 V.
Immerse the membrane in Ponceau-staining-solution and stain for 5 min.
Rinse membrane with distilled water until the background is clear.
Incubate in 5% milk in TBST (blocking solution) for 1 h at 18°C–25°C or for 14 h at 4°C with shaking.

Incubate membrane with primary antibody according to manufacturer's instructions in blocking solution for 2 h at 18°C–25°C or 14 h at 4°C with shaking: Upper part of membrane (> 50 kDa): ATGL (1:2000). Lower part of membrane (< 50 kDa): β-actin (1:2000).
Wash membrane 3 × 10 min with TBST at 18°C–25°C.

Incubate membrane with secondary antibody in blocking solution for 1 h at 18°C–25°C: Upper part of membrane (> 50 kDa): swine anti-rabbit HRP (1:2000). Lower part of membrane (< 50 kDa): goat anti-mouse HRP (1:2000).
Wash membrane 1 × 15 min and 3 × 10 min with TBST at 18°C–25°C.
Prepare 1 mL of ECL solution by mixing 500 μL of each solution.
Use different pipette tips for each solution.
Transfer membrane onto a clean surface (e.g., plastic foil).
Pipette ECL solution onto the membrane, distribute evenly and incubate for 1 min.
Wrap the membrane into a clean plastic bag and fixate it into the film-cassette.
Remove excessive ECL solution.
Detect the HRP-generated signal by applying a CL-XPosure Film on the membrane for 10 s to 30 min.
Protect the undeveloped film from light.
Develop the film using a Curix 60 X-ray development machine.
Draw protein ladder bands onto the film, before removing the membrane from the film-cassette.
Air dry the membrane and store it at −20°C for later repeated use.
